Variants.Content: Rhine, Danube, Britain and Africa have different supply networks linked by ports, crossings and roads. Storms, broken bridges and unrest become shortages elsewhere.

Rhine, Danube, Britain and Africa have different transport networks. Travelers and guards use specific banks, entrances and stops; outward access does not ensure return. Ports, crossings and roads connect western theaters.

Ports, crossings and roads connect western theaters. Passage relations need actual protection for adjoining sections; proximity does not equal a shared guarantee. Rhine, Danube, Britain and Africa have different transport networks.

Rhine, Danube, Britain and Africa have different transport networks. Closed routes may separate families from goods, imposing costs on those remaining at home. Ports, crossings and roads connect western theaters.
